name: 🧰 Ready for heca-pro — the pieces heca-pro builds on
description:
What open heca must provide so heca-pro (the commercial edition, private repo `~/projects/heca-pro`) can be built on top of it. Everything here helps any heca user too, which is why it lives in open heca and not in heca-pro. Agreed with Antonio on 2026-09-29; heca-pro's design is in `~/projects/heca-pro/docs/` (`decisions.md`, `open-heca-work.md`). **This feature's own accepted decisions (server/client model, several windows per session, sessions) override heca-pro decisions 6-7.**

heca keeps working on its own remaining features; this feature runs alongside and depends on no other feature.

## The model (see the accepted decisions)
heca runs standalone or as a server. The server holds every session (instance): workspaces, panes, running terminals and agents. A window is a client attached to one session; it can switch sessions in the same window, and draws everything (terminals, sidebars, docks, overlays) from data the server sends. Closing a window leaves the session running. Standalone = server + one client in one process. Sessions are saved as JSON and restored.

## Starting Point Before F012
- `heca` is a program only (`heca/Cargo.toml:2`); `HecaApp` private (`heca/src/main.rs:50`).
- `heca/src/app_state.rs` mixes window/renderers/retained chrome with session and backends.
- Terminal data is already separate from drawing (`heca-core/src/backend/snapshot.rs`: TerminalSnapshot, TerminalDamage).
- RPC language exists (`heca/src/rpc.rs`); nothing listens.
- One config file (`heca-config/src/loader.rs`); no project settings.
- No agent status (`heca-core/src/backend/terminal/osc.rs:4`, `heca-core/src/runtime.rs:72`).
- The drawing layer has no lines (`heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs:304`).
- The palette's mode table is written twice (`heca/src/chrome/palette.rs` ~370 and ~414).
- Save pattern to reuse: `heca/src/search_state.rs` (T386).

## Phases, in order
1. P098 — heca as a library with an entry point for adding things.
2. P104 — split into server and client, still in one process.
3. P099 — the connection: clients attach over a local socket; detach/attach; several windows per session; `heca rpc` for scripts.
4. P100 — sessions: palette `#` mode (after making the mode table one list, T526), session actions, CLI, plain `heca` attaches to the last.
5. P105 — save and restore sessions as JSON.
6. P101 — per-project settings (`.heca/config.toml`).
7. P102 — agent contract, agent status in the pane row, sounds (tasks moved from the old F008).
8. P103 — widgets: lines/arrows, tree layout, multi-line input, message list.
P101, P102 and P103 do not depend on the server work and can be done in any order.

## Rules for every phase
- AGENTS.md § 0 in full: pre-flight per type, widget vs component, DOM-shaped events, Rule Zero.
- Nothing hard-coded; never fix at the call site; a component owns its input and works wherever it is placed; placement is a dock the user places.
- One way in: the socket is the single door for outside commands, reading the ActionCatalog.
- Agent programs and roles are never a fixed list.

## Session Lifecycle And Recovery (Approved 2026-10-27)
The canonical details are in this feature's lifecycle and configurable-recovery Accepted Decisions.
- P100/T522 owns named sessions, attach/switch, launch-data capture and distinct Terminate / Restart / Delete actions.
- Terminate retains a stopped session and leaves its clients open with Session unavailable, [Restart] [Exit]. Restart is explicit. Delete removes Heca-owned session references and closes its clients, never project files.
- P105/T527 saves layout, lifecycle, original executable/arguments/cwd and native harness session/driver IDs in JSON.
- config.toml defaults resume_programs=true and resume_harness=true. Categories are independent. Registered drivers construct native harness resume commands; there is no universal --sessionId flag.
- GUI startup starts a missing server without a terminal. Server loss keeps existing windows open with the agreed dialog; neither reconnect nor startup silently resurrects intentionally terminated/deleted sessions.
- When resume is disabled, retain the pane/layout and initialize that content's normal fresh default: terminal shell, configured browser home, editor without files. All future registered content uses the same open factory/lifecycle contract; defaults are owned by each content's config, not a recovery-specific type list.
- P105 consumes managed-content creation/restore ownership in P094/T452 and the P067/T398 factory foundation without duplicating their registry or implementing Browser/Editor here.
- These are planned contracts, not completed implementation. Permanent-delete CLI spelling remains open.

acceptedDecisions.title: Two windows on one session share the content but move independently; terminal size is decided per pane (setting, default latest)
acceptedDecisions.decision: Shared (server): workspaces, columns, panes, terminals, agents, status, rooms, messages, notifications — a split made in one window appears in the other. Per window (client): which workspace is shown, focused pane, view scroll, open overlays/menus/palette, which docks are shown and where. Typing goes to the pane that window has focused; two windows typing into one pane both reach it. A "follow" option makes one window mirror another. A running terminal has one size: when several windows show the same pane at once, a setting decides — `smallest` | `latest` (window last typed in) | `largest`, default `latest`. A pane shown by only one window takes that window's size.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Agreed with Antonio 2026-09-29. Watch agents on one screen while working elsewhere; the window you type in gets the full size; a setting, not hard-coded.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: heca-core already separates terminal data from drawing: heca-core/src/backend/snapshot.rs TerminalSnapshot (:194) + TerminalDamage (:40, which rows changed). Over the connection send snapshot + changed rows; pixel cell sizes are the client's (font), rows x cols come from the attached windows.

acceptedDecisions.title: Sessions: palette `#` mode, CLI flags, plain `heca` attaches to the last session, saved as JSON
acceptedDecisions.decision: Command palette gets a sessions mode with sigil `#` (beside `:` commands, `@` panes, `$` workspaces): one row per session (name, project folder, windows attached, agents running); picking one switches this window; searchable and remembered like the other modes. Create / rename / terminate / restart / delete / detach are distinct actions (palette, key, RPC). CLI, in the cli.rs flag style: `heca --sessions [--json]`, `heca --attach <name>`, `heca --new <name> [folder]`, `heca --kill <name>`, `heca --standalone`. Plain `heca`: if a server runs, attach to the last session used; if none, start the server in the background, restore saved sessions, attach to the last. `--standalone` = today's behaviour, everything ends with the window. Sessions are saved and restored as JSON, reusing the search-history persistence pattern (`heca/src/search_state.rs`, T386: data_dir, version, atomic write, never fails on a bad file, saves when a revision changes). Restore rebuilds workspaces and panes; program relaunch and native harness resume follow the feature's configurable recovery decision. Running processes are not frozen. Intentionally terminated sessions remain stopped until explicit restart; deleted sessions are not restored.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Agreed with Antonio 2026-09-29. The palette is where users already switch panes and workspaces; one persistence pattern, not a second.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes:
The palette's mode table is written twice today: sigil_for (heca/src/chrome/palette.rs ~370) and the .mode(...) calls in open_command_palette (~414). Make it one table both read, so a new mode (sessions, or a plugin's) is declared once; do it with the sessions mode.
The 2026-10-27 lifecycle and configurable recovery decisions refine this overview. P100/T522 owns session lifecycle and client effects; P105/T527 owns durable state and relaunch/resume. --kill <name> means terminate, not permanent delete.

acceptedDecisions.title: heca runs standalone or as a server; the server holds every session, a window is a client
acceptedDecisions.decision: heca can run as a server holding all state: every session (instance) with its workspaces, columns, panes, running terminals and agents. A window is a client attached to one session; it can switch to another session in the same window. The client draws everything - terminals, sidebars, docks, overlays - from data the server sends; the server sends state and changes, never interface. Closing a window leaves its session and programs running (detach / attach, like tmux). Standalone = server and one client inside one process, so there is one code path. This replaces the earlier plan of one heca process per instance with OS-level window switching (heca-pro decisions 6-7).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Agreed with Antonio 2026-09-29. Agents keep running when the window closes; switching sessions in one window; one place for all state (one agent-comms member, one planner server for heca-pro); several windows on one session; attaching from another computer later. Cost accepted: splitting AppState and one crash affecting all sessions.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Order inside F012: library (P098) -> split server/client in one process (P104) -> connection over the socket with detach/attach and several windows (P099) -> sessions (P100) -> save/restore (P105). Split AppState once: today heca/src/app_state.rs holds renderers, window and retained chrome beside session and backends (81 files use AppState). SharedChromeState is the natural start for what the server sends. Actions are sorted into server (change state) and client (window only). The socket stays local only for now; clients from other computers need login and encryption and are later work.

acceptedDecisions.title: Another crate declares one extension name; its actions and layers are named under it
acceptedDecisions.decision: A program built on heca declares its identity once: `let pro = heca::extension("pro")`. Actions and layers hang off that handle and are named `<name>.<short>` (`pro.action("start_worker")` is `pro.start_worker`; `pro.layer("planner")` is `pro.planner`). The owner half is never written per item. `heca` is reserved for the app's own names and is refused. A short name that contains a dot is refused. A second extension with the same name is refused and reported. Docks keep their own `kind()` as their owner, unchanged. A future WASM plugin gets its name from its manifest, through the same handle. The extension name can be `pro` or `heca_pro` (Antonio, 2026-09-30).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Agreed with Antonio 2026-09-30. It keeps the existing rule that the owner half of a layer or action name is never an author's free string (heca/src/chrome/layers/layer.rs `layer_name`), so two extensions cannot claim each other's names and nothing can claim `heca.*`. One declaration per program instead of a prefix repeated on every item; pane decoration by name (T520 step 3) and later plugins use the same handle.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Replaces the first free-string doors `heca::action("id")` and `heca::layer("owner.short")` in heca/src/entry/ (built earlier in T520). Registration goes through the same queues and the same ActionCatalog / register_named_layer paths; only how the name is formed changes. Server side: actions. Client side: layers and pane decoration. Test: two extensions with one name, a dotted short name, and the reserved name are each refused and reported.

acceptedDecisions.title: A window's view lives in the window; the server only remembers the last view
acceptedDecisions.decision: Session is split so that the shared content (workspaces, columns, panes) stays in the session, and each window's view moves into a per-window value held by the client: the workspace shown, the workspace-switch animation, the scroll for each workspace, viewport size and scale. Layout math is shared and takes that view as an argument. The server stores only plain data: the last view per session, so that a newly attached window, or a restore, starts from it. A full layout copy per window and server-held views were both rejected.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio, 2026-10-02: the what was already decided (463ccd07), and he said to go with option 1 (stream2's A). It fits 463ccd07 (content shared, view per window), d108b88c (the server sends state, never interface, and holds no client state) and the save/restore decision. A layout copy per window would drift out of sync. Server-held views would put per-frame work and animation clocks on the server.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Two PRs. (1) Move ViewOffset, active workspace, switch, viewport and scale out of Session/ScrollingSpace (heca-core layout session.rs, scrolling.rs, workspace.rs) into a WindowView that the engine takes by reference. With one window the numbers are identical, so every layout test stays green. (2) The server/client door for layout changes (split, close, move…), named from the action catalog. This also unblocks moving PaneFacts / Server::facts / Change::FactsChanged behind the server (left over from P104 step 2c). Plugin lines are unchanged: a layer reads the shown workspace through its context, never through an id. Full options are in .planner/docs/handoff-p104-stream2.md.

acceptedDecisions.title: Terminate retains a stopped session; delete removes it and closes clients
acceptedDecisions.decision: Normal OS launch starts the server when needed, without a terminal. On server loss, keep windows open with a blocking Dialog: Restart and reconnect or Exit; disconnected windows do not restart it automatically. Terminate stops one session's processes but retains its saved definition and stopped state. Its clients stay open with Session unavailable and [Restart] [Exit]; only explicit Restart reactivates it. Delete stops the session, removes its saved definition and Heca-owned references, and closes its attached clients. Other sessions are unaffected. Project files are never deleted.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio distinguished termination from deletion and specified their client behavior on 2026-10-27.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: T522 owns lifecycle/actions/client handling. T527 owns durable stopped state and removal from JSON. No arbitrary session fallback or automatic resurrection.

acceptedDecisions.title: Configurable program relaunch and native harness resume from saved launch data
acceptedDecisions.decision:
config.toml provides resume_programs: bool = true and resume_harness: bool = true. These independently control ordinary programs and registered harnesses. Preserve each launch's executable, complete arguments and working directory in session JSON. For a harness also persist its driver identity and native session ID, distinct from Heca's session ID. When enabled, restart using the original launch data; the harness driver constructs the correct CLI resume invocation for that harness and saved ID. There is no universal --sessionId flag. Restore layout independently of these flags. An intentionally terminated session stays stopped until explicit Restart; Delete removes its definition and Heca-owned references, preventing later restore.
When resume is disabled for a category, keep the pane/layout but initialize its registered content at its normal fresh default, not an inactive placeholder: terminal-hosted program/harness becomes the user's normal shell; browser opens its configured default home page; editor opens with no files. Every future content type uses its own default constructor/factory contract, with defaults from its own config. Never hardcode a Terminal/Browser/Editor list or replace unrelated content with Terminal.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio approved configurable program/harness recovery and chose true for both defaults on 2026-10-27. This supersedes shell-only recovery and the earlier harness-only proposal. Antonio clarified fresh defaults for terminal, browser, editor and all future content when resume is disabled.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: P100/T522 owns lifecycle and launch/content identity capture; P105/T527 owns JSON and recovery policy. Use the open managed-content lifecycle/factory contract owned by P094(F011)/T452, consuming P067(F003)/T398; do not build a second registry or Browser/Editor implementations inside T527. Save launch argv/cwd and native harness IDs structurally. If resume is enabled, missing IDs, unsupported APIs or invalid targets are observable failures, not silent fresh conversations. If resume is disabled, fresh default content is the intended policy, not error fallback. Verify terminal behavior and a registered nonterminal/custom fixture so future content needs no recovery call-site special case.
